pages.text: Niobium and tantalum are twins, as zirconium and hafnium are, and lie together. Pyrochlore, (Na,Ca)2Nb2O6(OH,F), brown octahedra in carbonatite, is nearly all the niobium there is: Araxá in Brazil, a weathered carbonatite, gives about nine tenths of it.
pages.title: Niobium and tantalum

pages.text: Columbite-tantalite, (Fe,Mn)(Nb,Ta)2O6, black and heavy, is the tantalum mineral of the lithium pegmatites, Greenbushes' and Pilgangoora's, and with the Congo's coltan most of the world's tantalum.

Washed under a fan, raw pyrochlore leaves half its weight as concentrate. Araxá does not make niobium metal: it makes ferroniobium, about two thirds niobium, by aluminothermic reduction. Two concentrate, two aluminium powder and a raw hematite, lit over a superheated burner, burn on by themselves to two ferroniobium and a slag.
pages.title: Ferroniobium

pages.text: Nine tenths of niobium goes into steel, a few hundredths of a per cent, as microalloying: it pins the grain small and makes high-strength low-alloy steel, HSLA, for pipelines, bridges and car bodies.
pages.title: HSLA steel

pages.text: A ferroniobium nugget in two steel blocks, superheated, makes eighteen HSLA steel, about a tenth of a per cent niobium; an ingot of it presses to two heavy plates, being stronger at the same weight.

Two columbite dust, a potash, 500 mB of hydrofluoric acid and 250 mB of sulfuric acid, heated, are the digest and the MIBK solvent extraction in one step: the tantalum leaves as potassium fluorotantalate, K2TaF7, crystallised with the potassium chloride, Marignac's salt, and the niobium as its oxide, which goes to ferroniobium as pyrochlore's does.
Two fluorotantalate, two sodium and 100 mB of argon, superheated, reduce to a tantalum ingot: sodium reduction, the way nearly all tantalum powder is made.
pages.title: Sodium reduction

pages.text: Sodium comes from the Downs cell: two salt and a calcium chloride, which lowers the melt to about 600 °C, on two electrodes in a heated vat give a sodium ingot and 250 mB of chlorine, and the calcium chloride nine times in ten.

Euxenite carries niobium and tantalum too, and hydrofluoric acid takes them while the rare earths stay behind as fluorides: two euxenite dust digested the same way give a niobium oxide, a fluorotantalate one time in four, and a heavy rare earth concentrate.
pages.title: From euxenite and loparite

pages.text: Loparite is chlorinated, as Solikamsk does it: two loparite dust, a coal coke and 1,000 mB of chlorine, heated, give a niobium oxide, 250 mB of titanium tetrachloride and 250 mB of crude rare earth liquor.

Tantalum's oxide film is the thinnest, toughest dielectric there is, so most tantalum goes into capacitors: a tantalum nugget with a raw pyrolusite, the manganese dioxide cathode, a graphite and a silver nugget deployed on it in turn assembles into four capacitors.
pages.title: What it is for

pages.text: A tantalum nugget in the superalloy melt makes nine ingots where it made seven.

Sources: USGS, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025, Niobium and Tantalum; CBMM, "Niobium technical information"; Habashi, Handbook of Extractive Metallurgy (Wiley-VCH, 1997), Niobium and Tantalum; Gupta and Suri, Extractive Metallurgy of Niobium (CRC, 1994).
